messages:
Marta R: Quick sync — prototyping a compact "cost flipbook" card for the console. idea: a single card that can flip between per-token raw burn, amortized cache-savings, and per-model/unit econ. goal is fast compare across canary vs stable.
Jamal: Ooh. can we make the flip preserve the time window & sampling context? main pain today is the view switches windows and we lose the cohort filter.
Marta R: yes — preserving cohort. thinking of a compact state model: {view: 'raw'|'amortized'|'model', sample_rate: 1|0.1|0.01, cohort_id}. quick proto: ```json
{
  "view": "amortized",
  "sample_rate": 0.1,
  "cohort": "canary-2026-03-20"
}
```
Ash: love the proto. UX q: when flipping to amortized, how do we surface cache attribution uncertainty? we should show a confidence badge or +- range so PMs don't misinterpret small deltas.
Sana: agree. also routing matters — if the canary was sticky to a dedicated pool, cache warmness will bias savings. we need to surface 'routing skew' so users can judge whether prefetch/cache differences are from model or from routing.
Marta R: good point. proposal: two-line meta under the header: "routing skew: low/med/high" + a tooltip that links to the sample of recent routing policies for that cohort. plus a toggle to "normalize for routing" which applies a weights correction.
Jamal: how expensive is compute to normalize? doing it live at 1% sample seems fine, but at full resolution we might require a pre-agg job. maybe default to sampled quick estimate + "request full recompute" button.
DevEx Bot: Reminder: metric names must match the telemetry contract. Use tokens_total, tokens_cached, cache_hits, model_sku_cost. See spec: https://redwood.internal/telemetry/metrics/v2
Ash: UX: also let users pin a promptset comparison — e.g., compare the same promptset across models/canary. that will help QA isolate quality vs cost tradeoffs.
Sana: for the normalization algorithm, I sketched something: compute a routing weight per-tenant by inverse of fraction routed to dedicated pools during window, then adjust cache savings proportionally. rough psuedo:
```
for tenant in window:
  routing_bias = frac_to_dedicated(tenant)
  adjusted_cache_savings = raw_savings * (1 - routing_bias * alpha)
```
alpha can be tuned by experiments.
Marta R: neat. can the ops team expose frac_to_dedicated per cohort? ops-bot: pinged infra team to check.
ops-bot: @SRE Oncall FYI — can we export routing-destination breakdowns per cohort for last 7 days at 1h granularity? low-priority but helpful for console features.
Sana: if ops can provide that, we can precompute the normalized view nightly and keep a quick sampled live estimate.
Jamal: one last internal API question: do we want the flipbook to hit the same backend endpoint with a query param (view=amortized) or separate endpoints? my preference: single endpoint with mode param so caching + auth is consistent.
DevEx Bot: NOTE: new endpoint must be added to SDK changelog. @Marta R file a quick RFC.
Marta R: will do. next steps: I’ll sketch API, add a prototype card in dev console, and attach a small experiment plan for alpha users. anything else? :thinking_face:
Ash: add a small banner about uncertainty when sample_rate < 1. :+1:
Jamal: also add a "compare to historical baseline" small sparkline — makes diffs clearer.
Marta R: perfect. thanks everyone — I'll drop the proto link in this thread when ready.
root_message_text: proto for a compact 'cost flipbook' card that toggles per-token, amortized cache-savings, and per-model econ; asking about routing normalization, sampling, and API shape
